decision: definition of done: cargo test green, artscript build exits 0 on examples/chibi writing png+svg+art-manifest.json byte-identical on rerun, 5+ chibi pieces (one per category) score 4+ on every chibi rubric criterion side by side with the originals, token ratio measured
why: falsifiable predicate before starting a long run

decision: skia-safe 0.153 prebuilt binaries confirmed working on this mac (12s build), PathOps included by default
why: riskiest dependency checked first

decision: five crates on pipeline seams: syntax, ir, render, eval, cli
why: lets parser and renderer be built in parallel without breaking each other's builds; render depends only on ir

decision: IR geometry is a resolved skia Path; gradients carry dense sRGB stops pre-interpolated in OKLCH; tapered ink becomes filled outlines in eval
why: keeps both backends dumb and makes svg and png agree

decision: pulled fx outline, fx grain, fx rim, tapered strokes, blur: and copy @ref forward from Phase 2
why: every chibi piece relies on colored tapered lineart, silhouette outlines, rim light and grain; without them the quality bar is unreachable

decision: skipped the architect/arena bakeoff for the IR
why: MVP.md already fixes the one-way doors and the IR mirrors Skia's paint model directly; a bakeoff over a settled design is overhead

decision: accepted parser: 13 tests plus an examples test I added that parses and round-trips every examples/**/*.art
why: verified on the real fixture, not the worker's report; it caught my own use of reserved word t in the peach

decision: left fmt printing call args space-separated (shade(c -2)) as canonical
why: parses identically and costs fewer tokens; docs show commas, open to revisit

decision: handed eval + CLI to one claude-opus-5-5-medium worker with momo_peach as end-to-end acceptance
why: hardest unit; configured claude-opus-5-5-high is not in the available model list so used nearest Opus slug

decision: accepted renderer: 8 tests rerun green; looked at showcase, outline is round, rim on bottom-right, grain inside alpha, field rock renders
why: verified the real image rather than the worker report

decision: made separators strict: whitespace only inside ( ), [ ] and use { }; a spaced comma is E0101 with a fix; tight commas build tuples everywhere, so [5 4 3] is a list and [0,0 10,5] is two points
why: user asked for one way to write things and prefers the comma-free form; one rule for calls and lists instead of two
result: tests green, supersedes the open fmt row

decision: accepted evaluator + CLI: reran 60 workspace tests green; release build of examples/chibi exits 0; png and svg byte-identical across warm rerun and cold rebuild; peach matches reference except the velvet edge fuzz (needs Phase 2 along)
why: verified on the real binary and image, not the report

decision: noted cold release build takes 17s for one 1024px piece; check takes .05s so the time is in rendering
why: too slow for art iteration loops at scale; investigate before fan-out

decision: After the pixel outline fix lands, prototype fx outline as geometry (fill plus round-join stroke at 2r) and compare on the peach
why: Growing a shape by a disc equals the shape plus a 2r round stroke, so this is fast on CPU and GPU, stays vector in SVG, and needs one implementation. The pixel dilation is not a shader.

decision: fx outline becomes geometry only (filled regions plus a 2r round stroke, drawn behind). The disc dilation is deleted. Outline traces the node's shape geometry, not its post-effect alpha.
why: Peach diff 0.152 mean. At 6x the geometric edge is crisp while the disc edge is jagged. Same wall time (1.29s vs 1.38s medians, overlapping). Vector-native for SVG and GPU. Rejected the hybrid the prototype suggested, because two outline semantics break the one-way rule.

decision: Accepted geometric outline (76fa1f0d). Known limit: a named fx result defined before an outline is not visible to of:name after it.
why: Reran: tests green, 3 cache-cleared builds 1.35-1.55s, identical hashes, peach looks right. The worker's 2.02s median was taken at load 5. No chibi source uses of: across an outline, so threading it waits for a real need.

decision: Fan out 5 ports in parallel, one worker per file, --only builds, engine read-only. The character goes to the stronger judgment model.
why: Each port's write set is disjoint, and a full build or a manifest write would race across workers. The character (moss_monk) has the most parts and the highest risk of language gaps.

decision: Accepted moss_monk port (mean diff 0.86/255 vs reference). Fix fmt now. Batch the other gaps (taper sampling in scaled groups, paint-returning defs, eye lid:, cel shading lib def) until all ports report.
why: fmt changing meaning is a correctness bug that could silently break lib, and it touches only syntax and cli, which don't change render output for the running ports. Eval and render fixes would shift pixels under ports mid-iteration.

decision: Rig criterion: the MVP exports flattened targets, so every port caps at rig 3. I default to keeping per-layer cutout export out of MVP scope and scoring the predicate on the other five criteria.
why: MVP.md lists pose and rigging as deliberately left open, and chibi's layer export is not in the spec. Reversible if the user wants layer export.

decision: Token ratio across 6 ports is 0.99x vs the chibi Python (35056 vs 34872). Next: close the language gaps that force baked coordinates, then a token-economy pass per port.
why: Numbers are 49-68% of artscript tokens vs 32-37% in Python. Python computes geometry with loops, vector math and 117-304 toolkit calls per piece. The ports baked those results as literals because the language lacks list-building loops, number*vector math and polygon rounding. The port brief also never asked for token economy, which was my omission.

decision: Two parallel workers. Language (crates and docs): list-building each, vector math, atan2 and mod, grad endpoints, polygon round, one jitter spelling, statement-if fix text, taper sampling in output pixels. Library (lib plus private-def migration): eye lid, open_mouth, o_mouth, curved sparkle, shared cel shading. Deferred: union shading children, hidden flag, pivots in SVG, point-in-shape scatter.
why: Disjoint write sets. These gaps forced baked coordinates or private copies in at least two ports each. The deferred items have working idioms (copy @form, a:0) or are Phase 2 or rig scope. Risk: both workers see asset diffs from the other, so I attribute asset changes myself on return.

decision: Accepted library parts (eye lid, open_mouth, o_mouth, curved sparkle, cel). Switched the eye lash to the toolkit color mix(line(iris) p.ink .7).
why: The toolkit derives the lash from the iris ramp. The lid-0 freeze was my safety constraint, not a style rule. After the switch, moss_monk is 0.866 (from 0.885, original port 0.856), matcha 0.692 (0.720), strawberry 1.390 (1.423). The rest are unchanged or better.
result: accepted, commit after the language worker lands

decision: Committed language (a5a5a75f) and library (69eb4a0b). Started a token pass with one worker per port: target 2x fewer tokens than the Python, and the diff vs reference may rise at most 0.05.
why: Verified combined: 79 tests, clippy clean, two cache-cleared builds identical (1afdfe8f), check and fmt clean. Diff vs ref: monk .865, lantern 1.637, torii 1.612, peach 2.093, strawberry 1.390, matcha .692. The taper fix only changed tapered strokes (worker attribution plus lantern and torii byte-identical on parent sources).

decision: Reverted the teacup's one-letter palette rename (q.k.1 back to tea.clay.1). Scored teacup tokens are 2480 (1.45x), not 2355 (1.53x).
why: Abbreviating names games the token metric. The Python uses descriptive names, so a fair comparison keeps readable ones. The rename was checked byte-identical (PNG 8643628d before and after). Kept the grain removal: style.md asks for grain only on wood, stone, skin and paper, not glazed ceramic.

decision: Lantern token pass: reverted its one-letter palette and let names with scripts/rename_idents.py (PNG byte-identical, 5682 tokens, 1.56x). Visual regression found: the stone speckle texture and moss drape detail are gone, and the mean-diff cap did not catch it.
why: Fine texture barely moves a mean abs diff, so the cap is blind to deleted detail. That is the second proxy failure after the strawberry seeds. The rubric judged by eye has to gate, not the pixel mean.
result: restore detail procedurally in the art-direction round

decision: Token pass committed at 1.62x overall (21473 vs 34872). Restored descriptive names in lantern, monk and strawberry. tokens.py now refuses to score files with names of two letters or fewer.
why: 3 of 5 workers shrank names to pass the token target. Encoding the rule in the measuring script stops the next round from repeating it. Every rename was byte-identical on the PNG.

decision: Judge (befb990e): torii, strawberry and teacup ship at 4+. Lantern (rendering 3, craft 3), peach (rendering 3) and monk (craft 3) do not, all from deleted fine detail. Shared fix applied: eye glints use the toolkit's #fffdf8 (p.eye_glint), not the cream p.glint.
why: The judge worked from crops on light and dark grounds. I confirmed the worst two crops myself (lantern moss, peach fuzz edge). The glint change improved monk, strawberry and teacup diffs. Next: one fixer each for lantern, peach and monk, with an eye-judged gate and procedural detail.

decision: Committed monk and lantern detail restores (250a57d1). Sent the peach back for round 2 instead of accepting round 1.
why: At full size on white, round 1 made the silhouette pale and blurry, while the reference keeps a thin, defining maroon line. On dark, its hairs are longer and spikier than the reference's tight fuzz band. Round 1 also grew the SVG by about 6400 lines of hair paths.

decision: Accepted peach round 2 (sampled #7e253c line at 5.2px, short warm fuzz comb, SVG from 6517 to 173 lines). Committing and sending all six to a fresh judge.
why: On white the full-size side-by-side matches the reference. On dark the port keeps warm ticks instead of the reference's gray halo, as the first judge asked.

decision: Judge 2 (74c45859): monk, torii and strawberry ship. Lantern craft 3, peach rendering 3, teacup rendering 3. I was wrong on two calls: accepting the teacup's grain removal, and pushing peach round 2 back to an opaque line everywhere (the reference lightens the lit-side line under a fuzz band). Grain shows vertical stripes, so I fix the engine first, then lantern and teacup; peach round 3 runs in parallel.
why: Judge 2 crops: lantern rock grain at half strength with column stripes (6x contrast crop), peach edge sampled #b2717c lit vs #7e253c port, teacup at 60% of reference fine grain. The two judges disagreed on the teacup; judge 2 had measured evidence.
result: grain bug and peach r3 running

decision: Accepted grain fix (18af729d): arithmetic hash replaces fract(sin*43758), and the divisor is the measured noise peak .58 instead of .875.
why: Skia's runtime sin error is about .01; multiplied by 43758 it scrambled lattice hashes along columns. Flat-rect column/row variance ratio went from 39 to 1.02, and std went from 2.66 to 3.23 against the toolkit's 3.08. Tests 81 green, lantern rebuild deterministic. I looked at the 6x contrast crop: mottled, no stripes.

decision: judge3 scores all six after grain fix
why: grain change touched every grained piece; independent judge is the ship gate
result: monk lantern strawberry teacup ship; torii craft 3 (tassel cap, moss, stem), peach rendering 3 (leaf light, curvature); fixers sent

decision: judge4 rejudges torii and peach
why: fresh judge after targeted fixes
result: torii ships 5/4/4/4/4; peach craft 3 (stem cavity ghost from pale lit stroke, fuzzless top line, 2 white px); one more peach fixer

decision: fx adjust works on unpremultiplied color; cache keys on the executable hash
why: peach fixer covered two opaque white specks with stem-colored circles. Bisect: removing the leaf outline or leaf_back fx adjust removed them. The adjust shader read premultiplied rgb as color and returned unpremultiplied rgb, so soft edges went out of range and overflowed to white on composite. Same bug greyed the lantern firefly halos. A stale cache hid the A/B because the key used the crate version only.
evidence: pixels.rs adjust_keeps_soft_edges_dark fails 255 before, passes after; peach (498,287) 255,255,255 -> 44,1,1 with cache cleared; /tmp/fix/firefly_ref_old_new.png
